local.heading: Warner Robins grew up around the base, and the base is still hiring.
paragraphs: Warner Robins exists because of the base. In 1942 the farm community of Wellston took the name of Gen. Augustine Warner Robins, the same year the Army opened its air depot next door. The town became a city in 1956 and has kept growing since. Between the 2010 and 2020 censuses, Warner Robins added more than 20% to its population, and it now spreads into both Houston and Peach counties.

Robins Air Force Base is still the center of gravity. At the 2026 State of the Base, leaders said more than 21,000 people work there and the workforce grew 11% over the previous two years, with more growth expected. The Warner Robins Air Logistics Complex handles depot maintenance and engineering for the F-15, C-5, C-130, and C-17. The base hosts more than fifty organizations, which keeps a steady stream of contractors, suppliers, and new households coming to town.

Off base, business runs along a few long roads. Houston Medical Center, the 237-bed hospital at the center of the Houston Healthcare system, sits on Watson Boulevard. Central Georgia Technical College, Middle Georgia State University, and Mercer all run branch campuses in town. The Museum of Aviation next to the base is the largest tourist attraction in Georgia outside Atlanta, which brings visitors who need somewhere to eat and stay.

Downtown is changing too. Through Operation Reawaken, the city has been buying and clearing old buildings around Commercial Circle, starting on Watson Boulevard. In March 2025 it released renderings, drawn with UGA's Carl Vinson Institute of Government, for a walkable downtown with shops and homes. If you plan to open in that district, have the website and Google profile ready before the doors open. New customers in Warner Robins will look you up on a phone first.
